items.summary: No file in the tree states what a receipt that syncs after its float period closed does to that closed period, and the choice moves real money — so this is a product decision, not drift. Left unedited per owner-classification rules; brief below.
items.ownerBrief:
**Decision needed: what happens to a receipt that syncs after the float period it belongs to has already been reconciled?**

**Why it cannot be deferred to implementation.** The scenario is not an edge case the design tolerates — it is guaranteed by the design. 18.13.03 D-01 requires capture to work offline at the moment of spend ('Capture at the moment of spend, offline, in one photograph'), because thermal receipts are blank in three weeks (DT-02). Both reconciliation points are period-closing: 18.13.03:36 'At the end of the week the float reconciles: opening − payouts − receipts = the envelope' and 18.13.01:37 'At tour end the float reconciles: opening + income − payouts − receipts = what's in the envelope'. Offline capture plus a hard close means late arrivals are certain, and each of the three plausible treatments produces a different float balance and a different reimbursement owed to the person who spent the money. 18.13-tour-finance-cx.md:37 records this and says 'Unresolved' with no owner and no deferral target; none of the sub-domain's eight live Open Questions covers it.

**One asymmetry worth knowing before choosing.** The tree has already answered the same question for the *budget* and answered it the easy way: CX-02 synthesis Q5 says the budget 'is provisional throughout, and should say so rather than presenting a settled number' — a late receipt simply moves a number nobody had declared final. The float cannot borrow that answer, because reconciliation is the act of declaring the number final and handing over (or not handing over) cash. So the two objects legitimately need different rules, and the choice below is only about the float.

| Option | What it does | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A — Reopen the period** | The reconciliation reverts to open, the receipt posts to its true date, the variance and every reimbursement recompute | The books are true: the £40 the drummer spent on Tuesday is a Tuesday cost, and they are owed it | Reopening a settled week after cash has been handed out means asking for money back or issuing a correction; the TM's 'done' is revocable indefinitely, which is the state this whole sub-domain exists to end |
| **B — Post to the current open period, carrying its true spend date** | The closed period stays closed; the receipt lands in the open one as a prior-period item, visibly dated | Closure means something; the cost is never lost, only relocated; matches how real tour accounting actually runs a shoebox | Per-date P&L drifts — and 18.13.02 D-02 makes per-date the actionable grain, so a systematic bias toward late weeks is a real (if small) distortion of the signal the budget exists to give |
| **C — Absorb into the closed period's recorded variance** | The receipt explains part of the '£140 unaccounted' already booked; the variance shrinks, the total does not move | Closest to the existing rule at 18.13.01:43 — a variance is a first-class fact with a reason, and this gives it its reason retroactively | Only works when a variance exists and is large enough; and it silently changes a number the Producer already acted on, which CX-01 synthesis Q1 explicitly forbids elsewhere ('A system that silently balances is lying') |
| **D — Hard cutoff with an explicit grace window** | Late receipts post to the closed period for N days after close (A), and to the current period after that (B) | Bounds the revocability that kills A while keeping the books true for the common case — a receipt found in a jacket on Thursday | Introduces a number nobody has specified (N), and a grace window is a rule people must learn |

**Recommendation: D, with B as the fallthrough and A available only as an explicit, logged act.** Rationale: the failure this sub-domain is built to prevent is a float that reconciles by feel, so a receipt must never be discarded (rules out any 'write it off' reading of C as the default) and the variance must never move silently (rules out C outright). But a period whose closure can be undone by a background sync is not a closure, and reimbursements were paid against it. A short grace window keeps the honest case honest — most late receipts surface within days — and everything after it posts forward, dated truthfully, so the cost is never lost and the closed week stays closed. Reopening remains possible but becomes a deliberate, attributed action by the Producer rather than something a phone regaining signal does on its own.

**What you are actually deciding: (1)** which of A–D is the rule; **(2)** if D, the length of N (a working week is the obvious candidate but it is your call, not a derivable value); **(3)** whether a reopen — under any option — notifies the people whose reimbursements changed, which CX-01 synthesis Q4 already argues for in the ordinary case ('A reimbursement owed to someone should tell them').

**Where the answer belongs once made.** As a numbered decision in `18.13.03-expense-receipt-capture.md`'s Decision Log (it is the capture feature's late-arrival semantics), with an edge-case row alongside the existing 'Offline at a petrol station' row, and the CX-01 synthesis Q5 line at `18.13-tour-finance-cx.md:37` rewritten from 'Unresolved' to cite it. If you would rather park it, it needs registering as a sub-domain Open Question with owner User and a deferral target of `/create-prd` — the same shape as 18.13.01 Q-01 — because as written it is a deferral with neither.
